name: Tech Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public technology data.

entries.title: CAIDA Internet Measurement Datasets
entries.description: The dataset collection of the Center for Applied Internet Data Analysis (CAIDA) at UC San Diego: Internet topology (Ark traceroute, ITDK), BGP-derived AS relationships and prefix-to-AS mappings, network telescope and anonymized passive traces, among others. Some are public; many need an approved request.
entries.publisher: Center for Applied Internet Data Analysis (CAIDA), University of California San Diego

access.auth_note: Publicly accessible datasets download under the Public AUA; most other datasets need a data request approved by CAIDA under the Master AUA (one-year licence, CAIDA may refuse). Per-dataset access level is shown in the catalog

coverage.spatial: global Internet (topology, routing and traffic observed from CAIDA vantage points)
coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (e.g. pfx2as daily from 2005-05-09 for IPv4, 2007-01-01 for IPv6)

entries.license: restricted — CAIDA Acceptable Use Agreements: Public AUA (limited, non-exclusive, terminable licence; citation and publication reporting required) or Master AUA (non-profit research/education, commercial internal evaluation, or US Government purposes only)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (needed headless Chromium to render the listing). The old address https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/ redirects here. The catalog search page shows "Displaying 116 of 116" datasets with an Access filter (11 values) and a Status filter (84 "complete"). A sample dataset page, Routeviews Prefix to AS mappings (https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/routeviews-prefix2as/, HTTP 200), says "Files are created on a daily basis, starting from 2005-05-09 for IPv4 and 2007-01-01 for IPv6" in a tab-separated, line-oriented format, and "You are required to report your publications using this dataset to CAIDA." CAIDA is a research unit of UC San Diego (a university, not a federal agency), so this is not a US Government work. The "text" format reflects only the pfx2as sample; formats vary by dataset and were not surveyed. Cadence "irregular" because datasets update on different schedules.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the Master AUA (https://www.caida.org/about/legal/aua/) "applies to the majority of the CAIDA datasets, with the exception of datasets covered by the Acceptable Use Agreement for Publicly Accessible Datasets (Public-AUA)". It grants "a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, and terminable license to copy, modify, and use the data ... solely for the purpose of non-profit research, non-profit education, commercial internal testing and evaluation of the data, or for government purposes by or on behalf of the U.S. Government", effective "for a period of one year". The Public AUA (https://www.caida.org/about/legal/aua/public_aua/) grants "a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, and terminable license to copy, modify, and use the data in accordance with this Public Agreement" and requires the citation above plus reporting each publication to CAIDA. Neither is an open licence. Not checked: which datasets fall under which AUA, the request workflow, or any download limits.

entries.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog
entries.description: CISA's authoritative list of vulnerabilities known to be exploited in the wild, each with its CVE ID, vendor and product, date added, required action and due date, and known ransomware use. US federal agencies must remediate listed entries under Binding Operational Directive 22-01; it is widely used as a patch-priority signal.
entries.publisher: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), US Department of Homeland Security

coverage.spatial: global (vulnerabilities in products from any country, exploitation observed worldwide)
coverage.temporal: 2021-present (start year from the BOD 22-01 launch; not checked in the data)

entries.attribution: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 in headless Chromium; plain curl got HTTP 403 even with a browser User-Agent. The page says "CISA maintains the authoritative source of vulnerabilities that have been exploited in the wild", "The KEV catalog is also available in these formats: CSV JSON", links a "JSON Schema (updated 09-02-2026)" and a "License", and shows "Showing 1 to 20 of 1766 results". The JSON feed (https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json) returned HTTP 200 to curl with "catalogVersion": "2026.10.30", "dateReleased": "2026-10-30T17:02:45.3665Z", "count": 1766. The CSV is at https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/csv/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.csv (not downloaded). Cadence is "irregular" because entries are added as exploitation is confirmed, often several times a week. The 2021 start and the BOD 22-01 description are from background knowledge, not from pages read this session.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/licenses/kev/license.txt (403 to curl, HTTP 200 in headless Chromium): "The KEV database is distributed under the Creative Commons 0 1.0 License. You may use this data in any legal manner but note that information provided at any 3rd party links included in the KEV database are bound by the policies and licenses of those 3rd party websites. Use of the information does not authorize you to use the CISA Logo or DHS Seal". This is data-specific; as a federal agency work it would be public domain in the US anyway, and CC0 extends that worldwide.

entries.title: Cloudflare Radar Internet Traffic and Security Data
entries.description: Aggregate Internet trends observed across Cloudflare's network, served through the Radar API: HTTP request and NetFlow traffic, application- and network-layer attacks, BGP anomalies, DNS, and domain rankings, by country and network. A company-run source with an explicit (non-commercial) data licence.

access.auth_note: Free Cloudflare API token with Account > Radar > Read permission ("you must obtain your API token first")

coverage.spatial: global (traffic seen by Cloudflare's network; by country, region and autonomous system)

entries.license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Cloudflare Radar developer documentation, data-specific statement)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for the Radar developer documentation (https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/), which says "Using Radar's API you can access Cloudflare's data on global Internet traffic. Radar's API is free, allowing academics, technology professionals, and other web enthusiasts to investigate Internet usage across the globe." Its menu lists HTTP requests, NetFlows, application- and network-layer attacks, BGP anomalies (Beta), DNS and Domains ranking. The public dashboard https://radar.cloudflare.com/ returned HTTP 403 to curl and to headless Chromium ("Performing security verification ... protect against malicious bots"), so the docs page is catalogued as the canonical URL; the link checker will likely also be challenged on the dashboard. "Make your first API request" (https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/get-started/first-request/) says requests go to https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ with a Bearer token and shows format=json and format=csv parameters. Cloudflare is a commercial company, not a public body; jurisdiction national/US records its legal seat only, since the schema has no value for a company. Cadence "daily" is a placeholder; Radar data is near-real-time and the aggregation intervals were not checked. No API call was made (no token), so the history depth and rate limits are unknown.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the same docs page states "Data available via Radar API endpoints is made available under the CC BY-NC 4.0 license." This is explicit and data-specific, but non-commercial; it was found on the developer docs, not on the radar.cloudflare.com dashboard, which could not be read.

entries.title: Common Crawl Web Crawl Archives
entries.description: Monthly open crawls of the public web (about 2 billion pages and over 100 TiB compressed per crawl) as raw WARC captures, WAT metadata and WET extracted text, with CDXJ/URL indexes and host- and domain-level web graphs. A widely cited snapshot series of the web itself.

coverage.spatial: global (public web pages fetched by CCBot)
coverage.temporal: monthly archives 2013-present on the archive index page (latest CC-MAIN-2026-43, October 2026); earlier crawls not checked

entries.license: unverified — Common Crawl Terms of Use (rev. March 7, 2024) grant a "limited, non-assignable, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive" licence to use the Service; crawled pages "may be subject to separate terms" from their owners; no open data licence named
entries.attribution: Common Crawl Foundation, Common Crawl <crawl ID, e.g. CC-MAIN-2026-43>
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The Get Started page says the data "is hosted by Amazon Web Services' Open Data Sets Sponsorships program on the bucket s3://commoncrawl/, located in the US-East-1 (Northern Virginia) AWS Region. You may process the data in the AWS cloud or download it for free over HTTP(S)". The Latest Crawl page (https://commoncrawl.org/latest-crawl, HTTP 200) states "The latest crawl is: CC-MAIN-2026-43" and offers gzipped path lists of "WARC, WAT and WET files". The archive index (https://data.commoncrawl.org/crawl-data/index.html, HTTP 200), titled "Common Crawl Archives 2013-2026", says "The archives of the main crawl are released on a monthly basis" and lists CC-MAIN-2026-43 (October 2026, 2.16 billion pages, 109.20 TiB compressed). The site menu also lists a CDXJ Index, URL Index and Web Graphs; these were not opened. The Common Crawl Foundation is a US non-profit running a global crawl, recorded as international-ngo. The Internet Archive's Wayback CDX API was considered as a sibling entry but not written here.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Terms of Use, "LAST UPDATED: March 7, 2024" (https://commoncrawl.org/terms-of-use). "1. LIMITED LICENSE CC grants you a limited, non-assignable, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, limited license to access and use the Service subject to the terms and conditions of these ToU." It adds that the "Crawled Content" "may be subject to separate terms of use or terms of service from the owners of such Crawled Content", and lists prohibited uses (e.g. harvesting personal information, breaking the law). This is a service licence, not an open data licence, and the copyright in crawled pages stays with their owners, so re-users must check both. Not checked: rate limits on data.commoncrawl.org, the web-graph and index formats in detail, and the pre-2013 crawls.

entries.title: ENISA European Vulnerability Database (EUVD)
entries.description: The EU's vulnerability database, maintained by ENISA under the NIS2 Directive: publicly known vulnerabilities in ICT products and services with EUVD and alias identifiers (CVE, GHSA), CVSS scores, EPSS exploitation probability, exploited-in-the-wild flags and vendor data, including those coordinated by EU CSIRTs.

access.rate_limit: API responses capped at 100 records per search request (8 for the front-page endpoints); no request-rate limit stated

coverage.spatial: global (ICT products and services), with an EU CSIRT coordination focus

entries.license: unverified — no data-specific licence; ENISA website legal notice (site-wide) says "Reproduction of ENISA material published on this website is authorized, provided the source is acknowledged, unless it is stated otherwise"; much of the content is integrated from MITRE CVE and other sources
entries.attribution: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), European Vulnerability Database (EUVD)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for the HTML shell, but the page is a JavaScript app ("You need to enable JavaScript to run this app") and its contents needed headless Chromium. Rendered, it shows lists of "Critical vulnerabilities", "Exploited vulnerabilities" and "EU CSIRT coordinated vulnerabilities" updated within the last hours (e.g. EUVD-2026-114730, changed "1 hour ago"). The About page says "As per the NIS2 Directive, ENISA is mandated to develop and maintain the European vulnerability database", and the FAQ says it integrates data from "MITRE's federated CVE Program", vendor advisories and "CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerability Catalogue". The API page (https://euvd.enisa.europa.eu/apidoc) states "All endpoints are GET, require no authentication" with base URL https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu; a call to /api/lastvulnerabilities returned HTTP 200 application/json. No bulk download was found. Not checked: how far back records go, whether the record count matches CVE, and any rate limit beyond the per-request record caps.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no licence is shown on the EUVD pages or API docs. The EUVD footer links ENISA's Legal Notice (https://enisa.europa.eu/about-enisa/legal-notice/legal-notice, redirects to https://www.enisa.europa.eu/about-enisa/legal-notice), which covers "data, text, software and multimedia" on "the ENISA website" and says "Reproduction of ENISA material published on this website is authorized, provided the source is acknowledged, unless it is stated otherwise." It also says "the general principle is free access under open licenses" under ENISA's IPR policy, without naming one. This is site-wide, not EUVD-specific, and does not address the third-party (CVE, vendor) content, so the licence is left unverified.

entries.title: EPO Patent Bulk Data Sets and Open Patent Services
entries.description: The European Patent Office's raw patent data products: EP bibliographic and full-text data, the European Patent Register, the worldwide bibliographic (DOCDB) and legal event (INPADOC) databases, sequence listings, and Boards of Appeal decisions. The same data is available through the Open Patent Services (OPS) REST API, and it underlies Espacenet and most European patent analytics.

access.auth_note: free EPO account and subscription contract for bulk downloads; OPS needs registration and OAuth app keys (free up to 4 GB per week)
access.rate_limit: OPS: free up to 4 GB of data per week; above that an annual subscription (EUR 2 800) under the Fair use charter

coverage.spatial: European patents (EP), plus worldwide bibliographic and legal-event data from many patent offices (DOCDB, INPADOC)
coverage.temporal: varies by product (front files updated weekly; back files available)

entries.license: EPO terms and conditions for the licensing of EPO databases (licensed under contract with mandatory attribution; not an open licence)
entries.attribution: This product contains data sourced from EPO databases, © European Patent Organisation
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium), page "Bulk data sets | epo.org". It says "The EPO's bulk data sets are bulk extractions from EPO-internal patent databases made available to external users for further processing" and lists EP bibliographic data (EBD), the European Patent Register, EP full-text, DOCDB, INPADOC, sequence listings, national full-text data and Boards of Appeal decisions. The download platform, the Bulk Data Distribution Service (https://publication-bdds.apps.epo.org/raw-data/products, HTTP 200), needs an EPO account sign-in. Its public area listed "14.7 EPO worldwide bibliographic data (DOCDB) - front file Published at: 30.10.2026" and EP full-text data published 28.10.2026. The OPS page (https://www.epo.org/en/searching-for-patents/data/web-services/ops, HTTP 200) describes "a web service which provides access to the EPO's data via a standardised XML interface" and gives the conditions "'Non-paying' users Up to 4 GB of data per week Free" and "More than 4 GB of data per week Annual subscription: EUR 2 800". The page also points to PATSTAT for statistical analysis; PATSTAT is a separate paid product and is not cataloged here. Which bulk sets are free and which are priced was not checked, because the price list wasn't read. The XML format is assumed from the OPS documentation and DTD/Schema repository; individual product formats weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: "Terms and conditions for the licensing of EPO databases" (https://www.epo.org/en/service-support/ordering/raw-data-terms-and-conditions) says "The EPO databases are available only on a subscription basis" and "Where online access to and downloading of the EPO databases is free of charge, no payment is due". Licensees "must not use any address data included in the EPO database for advertising, promotional, spamming or other commercial purposes" and must include the statement "This product contains data sourced from EPO databases, © European Patent Organisation". The OPS terms (https://www.epo.org/en/service-support/ordering/terms-and-conditions/ops-terms-and-conditions) grant "a non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide licence to access OPS and use the data obtained via OPS", allow including the data in users' own products, and restrict making "the data as such" available. This is a contractual licence, not CC or public domain.

entries.title: Eurostat Digital Economy and Society Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU statistics on the digital economy and society, drawn mainly from the harmonised ICT usage surveys of households, individuals and enterprises. They cover internet access and use, broadband, digital skills, e-commerce, e-government, and enterprises' use of cloud, AI and other digital technologies across member states.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)
coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (individuals' internet use series from 2002)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium), page "Database - Digital economy and society - Eurostat", with "Comprehensive database", "Selected datasets" and "Detailed datasets" trees and tabs for Visualisations, Methodology and Legislation. The tree is collapsed in the page text, so the subject list in the description follows Eurostat's usual ICT-survey structure and wasn't read item by item. As a spot check, the dissemination API (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/isoc_ci_ifp_iu) returned JSON "Individuals - internet use", updated 2026-04-17, with time labels 2002-2025 (EU27_2020 share of individuals using the internet in the last 12 months: 94.53 for the latest year). Other formats are taken from Eurostat's general dissemination services and weren't checked. The R&D, innovation and patent tables are cataloged in science-almanac (eurostat-science-technology-innovation-database) and aren't duplicated here.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) says "The copyright for the editorial content of this website, which is owned by the EU, is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence" and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged." This matches the licence string used by the other Eurostat entries across the Almanac.

entries.title: FIRST Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) Scores
entries.description: A daily probability (0 to 1, with a percentile) that each published CVE will see exploitation activity in the next 30 days, maintained by the EPSS Special Interest Group at FIRST. Used alongside CVSS and the CISA KEV catalog to prioritise patching.
entries.publisher: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST), EPSS Special Interest Group

access.rate_limit: The API docs have a "Rate Limit" section that was not read; FIRST says the API "should not be used for bulk downloads" and points to the daily CSV instead

coverage.temporal: 2021-04-14-present (daily scores; model versions v1 to v5)

entries.license: unverified — no data licence named; the EPSS FAQ says scores "are published freely" with "no registration required" and "Attribution is requested"; the FIRST Services Terms of Use (site-wide) grant only a revocable licence for cybersecurity uses
entries.attribution: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST), Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS), https://www.first.org/epss
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The "Get the Data" page says "A single stable URL always points to the current day's complete file" and that it is "a gzip-compressed CSV containing three fields for every scored vulnerability: cve ... epss ... percentile". It lists model versions from "EPSS v1: scores begin 2021-04-14" to "EPSS v5 (v2026.06.15): started publishing 2026-06-15", and says "Scores are generated by Empirical Security and published freely to the community." The daily file https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz redirected (302) to epss_scores-2026-10-31.csv.gz (HTTP 200), headed "#model_version:v2026.06.15,score_date:2026-10-31T12:00:27Z". That host belongs to Empirical Security, FIRST's named score producer, linked from FIRST's own page, so it is the official distribution and not a mirror. The API https://api.first.org/data/v1/epss?cve=CVE-2021-44228 returned JSON with "access":"public" and a 2026-10-31 score. The data page also links a GitHub repository (github.com/empiricalsec/epss_scores), which was not opened.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the EPSS FAQ (https://www.first.org/epss/faq) answers "Is EPSS free to use? Yes. EPSS scores are published freely via CSV download and API with no registration required. Attribution is requested when EPSS data is used in publications or products." No specific attribution wording was found on the data page. The FIRST Services Terms of Use, Version 1.0.0 (https://www.first.org/about/policies/terms), grant "a nonexclusive, nontransferable, revocable, limited license to view, copy, print, and distribute Content retrieved from the Services ... only for vulnerability disclosure, cybersecurity incident response, or preventative cybersecurity uses". These are site-wide, not EPSS-specific, and it is unclear whether they cover the CSV hosted by Empirical Security, so no licence id is given.

entries.title: ITU DataHub (ICT indicators)
entries.description: The International Telecommunication Union's official global ICT statistics for about 200 economies: Internet use, fixed and mobile broadband subscriptions, mobile network coverage, traffic, ICT prices, household ICT access and use, and telecom regulatory information. It replaces the paid World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database.

coverage.spatial: Global (about 200 economies, plus world and regional aggregates)
coverage.temporal: varies by indicator (the query tool defaults to 2018-2026)

entries.license: CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0-IGO (ITU DataHub Disclaimer and Terms of Use)
entries.attribution: International Telecommunication Union, ITU DataHub, https://datahub.itu.int/ (with access date)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 202. Behind CloudFront: curl with a plain User-Agent got HTTP 403 ("Request blocked"), curl with a browser User-Agent got 202, and only headless Chromium rendered the page (title "The world's richest source of ICT statistics and regulatory information - ITU DataHub"), with Data explorer, Indicator catalogue and Data query sections. The About page describes "ITU Household ICT Indicators" and "ITU World Telecommunication Indicators" collections for "about 200 economies worldwide", collected through annual government questionnaires. The old database page (https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Statistics/Pages/publications/wtid.aspx, HTTP 200) says "The World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database was discontinued in 2024. All the data is now available free of charge on ITU DataHub subject to updated Terms of Use", so the paid WTID is not cataloged separately. ITU's statistics page (https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Statistics/Pages/stat/default.aspx) also offers global and regional Excel aggregates for 2005-2025. Download formats, any API, and start years weren't checked, so format is left empty. A Login link exists, but the query page loaded without one.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the DataHub About page (https://datahub.itu.int/about/#disclaimer-and-terms-of-use) says "The Data is licensed to the public through a Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO license. Under the terms of this licence, you may copy, redistribute, and adapt the Data for non-commercial purposes, provided the work is appropriately cited." The "terms of this licence" link, however, points to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/3.0/igo/ (BY-NC, without ShareAlike), so the ShareAlike term is uncertain. Third-party data on the DataHub follows its owners' terms. The data is non-commercial only.

entries.title: CVE List (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures)
entries.description: The authoritative list of publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities, one CVE Record per vulnerability, assigned by the CVE Program's worldwide CVE Numbering Authorities. The shared identifier that NVD, EUVD, KEV and EPSS all key on.
entries.publisher: The MITRE Corporation (CVE Program, sponsored by US DHS CISA)

coverage.spatial: global (vulnerabilities in products from any country)
coverage.temporal: program running since 1999; earliest record year not checked in the data

entries.license: CVE Terms of Use: perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright licence to reproduce, adapt and distribute, on condition that MITRE's copyright designation and the licence are reproduced in copies (not a US Government work; not a named open licence)
entries.attribution: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE™), Copyright © 1999-2026, The MITRE Corporation (reproduce MITRE's copyright designation and the CVE Terms of Use licence in any copy)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (www.cve.org is a JavaScript app; its content needed headless Chromium). The Downloads page says "The CVE List is available for download in the format below, per the terms of use" and that "Bulk download files of CVE Records in the CVE Record Format are hosted in the cvelistV5 repository on GitHub.com", with daily "Year-Month-Day_all_CVEs_at_midnight.zip" baselines and hourly delta zips; it notes legacy CSV, HTML, XML and CVRF downloads ended on June 30, 2024. The home page says "There are currently over 398,000 CVE Records". The GitHub repository (github.com/CVEProject/cvelistV5) is the program's own distribution point, not a mirror, but its release page returned HTTP 403 to this session, so the latest release was not confirmed. The CVE Services API was not checked. MITRE is a federally funded non-profit that runs the program under CISA sponsorship; jurisdiction national/US records that, although CNAs are worldwide.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: CVE Terms of Use (https://www.cve.org/Legal/TermsOfUse), "CVE Usage: MITRE hereby grants you a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright license to reproduce, prepare derivative works of, publicly display, publicly perform, sublicense, and distribute Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE™). Any copy you make for such purposes is authorized provided that you reproduce MITRE's copyright designation and this license in any such copy." The footer reads "Copyright © 1999-2026, The MITRE Corporation. CVE is a trademark ... of The MITRE Corporation." So CVE data is not public domain; the licence is permissive, with a notice-retention condition.

entries.title: Measurement Lab (M-Lab) Open Internet Measurement Data
entries.description: Open Internet measurement data collected by the M-Lab platform worldwide: NDT speed tests (download, upload, round-trip time, packet loss), traceroute and reverse traceroute paths, TCP INFO, packet headers and Wehe traffic-differentiation tests, plus monthly global summary statistics.

access.auth_note: Querying the enriched tables through Google BigQuery needs a Google Cloud account; M-Lab's own access steps were not checked

coverage.spatial: global (measurements between end-user clients and M-Lab servers worldwide)
coverage.temporal: NDT 2009-present; traceroute 2013-present; other datasets from 2018-2024 onwards

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (M-Lab Data Catalog, "Data License and Citing M-Lab Data")
entries.attribution: The M-Lab <test name> Data Set, <date range used>. <M-Lab test URL> (e.g. "The M-Lab NDT Data Set 2009-02-11–2015-12-21. https://measurementlab.net/tests/ndt")
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The Data Catalog page says "Open Internet measurement data released under CC0" and that data is published as "enriched data (parsed, annotated, and queryable via BigQuery or available as pre-computed summaries) and archival data (measurement logs on Google Cloud Storage)". It lists Monthly Global Stats (2009 – present), NDT (2009 – present), Packet Header (2019 – present), Reverse Traceroute (2024 – present), TCP INFO (2019 – present), Traceroute (2013 – present) and Wehe (2018 – present), most marked "Continuous". The publisher is M-Lab itself, which describes itself as "a fiscally sponsored project of Superbloom Design" (US) led by researchers with partner companies and institutions; jurisdiction is recorded as international-ngo because it runs a global platform and is not a government agency. Cadence "daily" stands in for continuous collection.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the same page (https://www.measurementlab.net/data/) states "All data collected by M-Lab tests are available to the public without restriction under a No Rights Reserved Creative Commons Zero Waiver" and that both enriched and archival data "are released under CC0 1.0 Universal". This is a data-specific statement; the site footer's CC-BY-4.0 covers original website material, not the data. Not checked: the BigQuery table names, the raw-archive file formats beyond the .pcap packet-header files, the summary download formats, and any rate limits.

entries.title: NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD)
entries.description: The US government repository of vulnerability management data built on the CVE List, adding NIST analysis such as CVSS severity scores, CWE weakness types and CPE product applicability, plus the CPE Dictionary and CPE Match data. Available through the CVE/CPE 2.0 APIs and JSON 2.0 data feeds.
entries.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

access.auth_note: Optional free API key raises the API rate limit
access.rate_limit: 5 requests per rolling 30 seconds without an API key, 50 with a key; NIST recommends sleeping six seconds between requests

coverage.spatial: global (vulnerabilities in products from any country)
coverage.temporal: yearly feeds from 2002 (the 2002 feed includes earlier CVEs) to present

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work) for NIST's own content; CVE descriptions inside NVD records come from MITRE's CVE List under the CVE Terms of Use
entries.attribution: National Institute of Standards and Technology, National Vulnerability Database. Services are asked to display: "This product uses data from the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD."
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (pages rendered with headless Chromium; plain curl to https://nvd.nist.gov/ also returned 200). The NVD Data Feeds page lists "CVE and CPE APIs", "2.0 JSON Feeds" (Vulnerability, CPE Dictionary and CPE Match feeds), translation feeds and vendor comments. It says "The 'year' feeds are updated once per day, while the 'recent' and 'modified' feeds are updated every two hours", and the CVE-Modified feed showed "Oct 31, 2026; 4:00:08 PM +0000" (GZ, 13.86 MB). The developers page (https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/start-here) gives the rate limits recorded above. A direct call to https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0 timed out after 20 seconds from this session, so the API itself was not confirmed. Not checked: the NIST Public Data Repository DOI for citation, and how far back the CVSS analysis goes.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the NVD developers page and the Data Feeds page say "All NIST publications are available in the public domain according to Title 17 of the United States Code, however services which utilize or access the NVD are asked to display the following notice prominently within the application: 'This product uses data from the NVD API but is not endorsed or certified by the NVD.'" The NVD General FAQ (https://nvd.nist.gov/general/faq-sections/general-faqs) repeats "All NIST publications are available in the public domain." NIST is a federal agency, so its own analysis is a US Government work. NVD records also carry CVE text that MITRE licenses under the CVE Terms of Use (see mitre-cve-list), so re-users of full records should keep MITRE's notice too.

entries.title: NTIA Internet Use Survey (CPS Computer and Internet Use Supplement)
entries.description: The US government's long-running survey of how Americans go online, fielded as a supplement to the Census Bureau's Current Population Survey. It covers internet use by location, devices, home connectivity, reasons for non-use and online activities, with public use microdata for every wave since 1998 and NTIA's summary Analyze Table.
entries.publisher: National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), US Department of Commerce
entries.attribution: NTIA Internet Use Survey (Current Population Survey Computer and Internet Use Supplement), National Telecommunications and Information Administration
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The page says "NTIA has made public use datasets available for every NTIA Internet Use Survey, as well as the Analyze Table of summary statistics used in the Data Explorer. All datasets are available in Stata, R, CSV, and raw/fixed formats, and are accompanied by official documentation produced by the Census Bureau". The newest wave listed is Nov 2023 (nov23-cps-*.zip, posted 08/30/2024), and waves go back to Aug 2000 in the download table. The NTIA Data Explorer (https://www.ntia.gov/data/explorer, HTTP 200) offers datasets from Dec 1998 to Nov 2023 by state, with "Full data set: ntia-analyze-table.csv". The guessed URL https://www.ntia.gov/page/ntia-internet-use-survey returned 404. The cadence is recorded as irregular: waves have been biennial since 2017 and irregular before that, and the schema has no biennial value. The file downloads themselves weren't opened.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no data-specific licence was found. NTIA's Web Policies page (https://www.ntia.gov/page/web-policies) covers linking and comments only and has no copyright statement. The data is collected for NTIA by the US Census Bureau, both federal agencies, and published by NTIA, so it is treated as a US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105). This is inferred from authorship, not from a stated licence.

entries.title: OECD.AI Policy Navigator (national and international AI policy database)
entries.description: The OECD.AI Policy Observatory's live database of public AI policies and initiatives from more than 80 jurisdictions and international organisations: national strategies, governance bodies, regulations, guidelines and standards, and programmes, filterable by status, legal bindingness, start year, sector and AI principle.

coverage.spatial: more than 80 countries, territories and international organisations
coverage.temporal: not checked (entries carry start years; the list is ordered by start year)

entries.license: unverified — the OECD.AI footer reads "© 2026 OECD. All rights reserved" and links OECD Terms and Conditions (oecd.org), which sat behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read
entries.attribution: OECD.AI (2025), OECD.AI Policy Navigator, accessed on <dd/mm/yyyy>, https://oecd.ai/dashboards
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (plain curl returns 200 but the page is a JavaScript app; content read in headless Chromium). The page says "Our policy navigator is a living repository from more than 80 jurisdictions and organisations" and "The navigator is a live database updated regularly by official contact points from countries and international organisations and OECD.AI experts." The All initiatives view (https://oecd.ai/en/dashboards/policy-initiatives) showed "List of policy initiatives (2637)" with filters for country, international organisation, category, status, legally binding, start year, type, AI principles, target sectors and AI tags. It gives the citation "Please cite as: OECD.AI (2025), OECD.AI Policy Navigator, accessed on 31/10/2026, https://oecd.ai/dashboards." No bulk download, export button or API was found, so access is recorded as web only. OECD.AI's separate "Live data" section (https://oecd.ai/en/data) shows AI research, jobs, investment, compute and patent visualisations built largely on third-party sources (OpenAlex, Scopus and others) and is not covered by this entry.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the OECD.AI footer reads "© 2026 OECD. All rights reserved" and links "Terms & conditions" at https://www.oecd.org/termsandconditions/. That page, and https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, returned a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (HTTP 403) to headless Chromium this session. Another Almanac entry (labor-almanac oecd-employment-labour-market) quotes those terms as allowing reuse of OECD Data "for any purpose, even for commercial use" with credit, but whether that covers policy-database entries submitted by national contact points was not confirmed, so the licence is left unverified.

entries.title: OECD Broadband and Telecom Databases
entries.description: OECD's broadband and telecommunications statistics for member and accession countries: fixed and mobile broadband subscriptions by technology and speed tier, and related telecom indicators collected from national authorities. They are the comparative series behind the OECD Broadband Portal.
entries.publisher: OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development)
entries.license: unverified — OECD terms page (oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html) is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and could not be read
entries.attribution: OECD, Broadband and telecom databases (OECD Data Explorer)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl). The Data Explorer is a JavaScript app and was read in headless Chromium, titled "OECD Data Explorer • Broadband and telecom databases". It says "This dataset represents a selection of 14 indicators, based on questionnaires received by the OECD from relevant national authorities of OECD members and accession countries", with "Number of unfiltered data points: 69634" and "Last updated: October 13, 2026". The default view is quarterly subscriptions. The SDMX API (https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/dataflow/OECD.STI.DEP/DSD_BB_DATABASE@DF_BB_TEL_DATABASE/latest) answered HTTP 200 for dataflow version 2.0. The same API also lists related OECD.STI.DEP flows, "ICT Access and Usage by Households", "...by Individuals" and "...by Businesses", which aren't cataloged separately. The OECD Broadband Portal pages on www.oecd.org (https://www.oecd.org/en/topics/sub-issues/broadband-statistics.html) returned a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (HTTP 403) to curl and headless Chromium, so this entry points to the Data Explorer instead. The formats are taken from the Download and Developer API buttons and weren't tested. The canonical URL's square brackets are percent-encoded.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: not verified. The Data Explorer footer links "Terms & conditions" to https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, which returned a Cloudflare 403 to headless Chromium and WebFetch this session. The labor-almanac oecd-employment-labour-market entry, checked the same day, quotes that page's "3. Data" section as permitting reuse "for any purpose, even for commercial use" with credit to the OECD, and says it is not CC BY 4.0. I did not read it myself, so no licence is asserted here.

entries.title: RIPE Atlas Internet Measurement Data
entries.description: Results of active Internet measurements (ping, traceroute, DNS, TLS/SSL, HTTP, NTP) run by the RIPE NCC's global network of RIPE Atlas probes and anchors, available through the RIPE Atlas API and as daily raw-data dumps.
entries.publisher: RIPE NCC (Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre)

access.auth_note: Public results can be read without an account; creating new measurements needs a RIPE NCC Access account and credits (not checked this session)

coverage.spatial: global (probe and anchor network, densest in the RIPE NCC service region of Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia)
coverage.temporal: daily dumps for roughly the last month (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30 seen); API served 2025 results when tested, start year not checked

entries.license: restricted — RIPE Atlas Service Terms and Conditions v3.5 (research and operational use; "Any commercial use of the RIPE Atlas Data is subject to prior permission by the RIPE NCC"); no open licence named
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for https://atlas.ripe.net/ and for the RIPE NCC's RIPE Atlas page (https://www.ripe.net/analyse/internet-measurements/ripe-atlas/), whose menu lists "RIPE Atlas Raw Data" under "Raw Datasets". The daily-dump index https://data-store.ripe.net/datasets/atlas-daily-dumps/ returned HTTP 200 with folders 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-30 (latest written 31-Oct-2026); a folder holds hourly bz2 files per measurement type (e.g. "connection-2026-10-29T0000.bz2"). That index only goes back about a month, so it is a rolling window, not an archive. The RIPE NCC is the Amsterdam-based Regional Internet Registry and membership association, recorded as international-ngo. An unauthenticated API call (https://atlas.ripe.net/api/v2/measurements/1001/results/ for a one-hour window on 2025-10-31) returned HTTP 200 application/json with ping results, so the API serves results at least a year old; how far back it goes was not checked. The dump files were not decompressed, so their inner format is unconfirmed.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: RIPE Atlas Service Terms and Conditions, "Version 3.5, Updated 26 September 2025, Effective as of 4 November 2025" (https://www.ripe.net/about-us/legal/ripe-atlas-service-terms-and-conditions/). Article 4.1: "The RIPE NCC will publish the RIPE Atlas Data in various forms and make this available via http://www.ripe.net/ ... as well as the RIPE Atlas API." Article 4.5: "Users agree to make responsible use of the RIPE Atlas Data in line with the purposes of the RIPE Atlas Service ... Users may perform research using RIPE Atlas Data ... Any commercial use of the RIPE Atlas Data is subject to prior permission by the RIPE NCC." Article 3.1 gives the purposes as "research, network monitoring, network debugging and alerting about network events". No Creative Commons or other open licence was found. RIPEstat, a separate RIPE NCC service, has stricter terms (no redistribution) and is not covered here.
